nv_sandy_corridor.blurb: Sandy Corridor is a small box canyon at Red Rock, tucked beside the Sandstone Quarry lot a short stroll away. It holds 14 routes, split between sport and trad, with a few top-ropes possible. Grades run wide: a single 5.7, a cluster of 5.9s and 5.10s, then a hard end with several 5.12s and 5.13s. The sandstone is brittle, so it should be left alone whenever it is damp. Trad lines mostly sit low on the walls and see little traffic, while the steeper sport lines are higher up. Expect a quieter visit than the sport walls nearby.

nv_rift_corridor_left.blurb: Rift Corridor Left is a sandstone sport wall in the Calico Hills section of Red Rock, and it holds most of the routes in the Rift Corridor. All 14 climbs are bolted, and the grades are friendly: a few 5.8s, five 5.9s, five 5.10s and a lone 5.11. The slot is tight for roughly the first thirty feet, then widens, with lines on both sides near the far end. Some of the best climbing is at the back. Because the slot funnels falling rock onto the person belaying, a helmet is a good idea.
nv_rift_corridor_left.approach: From the pullout lot, follow the main dirt path toward the cliff, drop into the gully under Circus Wall and keep right, then cut left through a gap in the scrub oak. Stay tight to the left wall for about twenty feet to reach the slot.

nv_burlap_buttress.blurb: Burlap Buttress is a broad sandstone ridge dividing the main forks of Black Velvet Canyon at Red Rock. Its 14 listed climbs are almost all trad, with one 5.7, a 5.8, four each at 5.9 and 5.10, and a few harder 5.11 and 5.12 lines. Getting there means following the usual Black Velvet trail, dropping into the wash and working west on faint trail threads, so it feels more remote than the canyon walls. The ridge is also a scrambling objective, and the terrain around it can be brushy.

nv_first_creek_slabs.blurb: First Creek Slabs is a string of ribs and buttresses along the south side of First Creek Canyon at Red Rock, beginning upstream of the Lotta Balls and Romper Room walls. The 14 climbs here are all trad and mostly long, running from three up to around ten pitches and gaining up to 1,500 feet. Grades are gentle, mainly 5.7 with a handful of 5.5 to 5.6 and a few 5.8 to 5.9 lines. Starting just above the streambed, it suits moderate parties willing to rappel many times on the way down. Sandstone here is delicate when wet.

nv_south_face_2.blurb: The South Face of Windy Peak, in the Windy Canyon corner of Red Rock, is a sun-catching wall of long trad routes, up to about eight pitches. Its 14 climbs are mostly 5.9 with a spread of 5.8s and 5.10s, one 5.7 and one 5.11. It is a committing day: the hike in from the dirt-road parking takes well over an hour, and routes finish on the summit ridge, from where cairns lead down a gully and back to the base. Crowds are rare and the wall gets plenty of sun, which makes it attractive in cooler months. Wind can be strong up high.

nv_hustle_wall.blurb: Hustle Wall is a bolted face on the Lower Cliffs of Sleepy Hollow, on the west side of Mount Potosi outside Las Vegas. All 14 climbs are sport routes, and it leans toward the harder end: one 5.8, three 5.10s, four 5.11s, five 5.12s and a 5.13. Most are short, around fifty feet, so it suits a quick session for someone climbing in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. The cliff is a very short walk from the car, and the routes start left of the point where you arrive.
